question: Does committing a rip-up only when its victims re-land (arm strict) or when the incomplete count strictly falls (arm count) leave fewer KiCad-unconnected items after pass 1 than Java's rip-up on at least N-1 eligible boards, with none worse, no new DRC errors and no via in a pad; and does it still win when both arms are followed by an Q10 sweep?
rule_text: each pair is judged by N02's totals rule (freerouting-dev gate --prereg on a records file per pair): hard metrics 0, guards not worse than the pair's baseline, no board worse than twice its band, and the summed signal improved by more than the set noise; pass_rule (the paired rule) is printed for each pair, not judged

mp1.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile

ripcost-best.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
ripcost-best.what: baseline: pass 1 at the start_ripup_costs Q11.1's no-code sweep {1500, 5000, 20000} and rip-up-off arm chose (fewest kicad_unconnected summed over the eligible boards, ties by fewest vias), written here as an amendment that changes nothing else before any wrapper arm runs; the later flag wins over the 1500 of the base command. If rip-up off wins, the arm is pass 1 with rip-up off (the flag the Q11.1 note names)

strict.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
strict.what: candidate: transaction, every victim net must re-land (Q11.2)

count.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
count.what: candidate: transaction, the incomplete count must fall (Q11.3)

depth1.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
depth1.what: candidate: count, victims may rip once, no net twice (Q11.4)

strict+ripfactor.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
strict+ripfactor.what: candidate: strict plus rip-count protection, rip cost times 1+2k (Q11.5)

mp1+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
mp1+sweep.what: baseline: as mp1, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

ripcost-best+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
ripcost-best+sweep.what: baseline: as ripcost-best, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

strict+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
strict+sweep.what: candidate: as strict, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

count+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
count+sweep.what: candidate: as count, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

depth1+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
depth1+sweep.what: candidate: as depth1, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

strict+ripfactor+sweep.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q11's code (one Linux release build for every arm); the default profile
strict+ripfactor+sweep.what: candidate: as strict+ripfactor, then Q10's add-only sweep (free, 2 passes)

pairs_rule: baseline_arm/candidate_arm name the primary pair for freerouting-dev gate; every pair is judged on its own by the totals rule; a candidate passes only if it passes against both mp1 and ripcost-best, and its +sweep arm is reported against mp1+sweep (the composed flow, Q00)

boards.eligibility: every board of tools/bench/sets/benchmark.txt, owner.txt and the 2-layer medium/hard rows of kicad-corpus.txt on which the unchanged engine at the registration commit (arm mp1) leaves at least one incomplete connection; the list goes into `eligible` below, as an amendment that changes nothing else, before any candidate arm runs. canary-pwr-9511d9a and pours1..3 count as one board (grouped, as in Q01.json).
boards.grouped: fixtures/canary-pwr/*.dsn are one board for pass_rule (the variants of one placement)
boards.board_flags: none beyond the arm commands; the canary-pwr flags are in every command (start_ripup_costs 1500, min_trace_width_um 150), as Q10.json uses them
boards.why: Q10's universe and eligibility rule: Q10, Q11 and Q12 are measured as one family (Q00), so they share the boards

grading: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh where a .kicad_pcb exists (copper severities forced to error, input DRC subtracted, refill on); canary-pwr by canary-23 (ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py)

metric_definitions.work_units: the run's maze work units (freerouting-dev bench record); a rolled-back attempt's work stays on the meter, so it is counted
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.unrouted: the router's final unrouted count (its log)

extra_reported: rip-stats (router.special.diagnostics=rip-stats): rips, reroutes, re-land share per arm
the job log's 'Transactional rip-up' tally: transactions, committed, rolled back, retries routed, victim nets, re-landed, re-rips refused
keep_rule: keep the best passing candidate as a setting (off by default, in no profile) only if it passes the totals rule against both mp1 and ripcost-best; with several passing, the fewest kicad_unconnected summed over the eligible boards, ties by fewest vias. A change to profile enhanced needs its own registration
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board after P04's default-tree decision; no reruns with other settings, rules, depths or factors
not_registered: rule strict with depth 1 (built and tested, not an arm)

decision_table.pass: keep the best passing arm as a setting (off by default); DIVERGENCES line
decision_table.fail: remove quality/transaction.rs and the ripup_factor hook; Q11.1's table and the numbers stay in Q11.6's done note

timing: measured only after P04's default-tree decision
